- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often over-forecasts; reduce forecast to reflect bearish bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% for the following 3–5 days.
- Model shows strong mean reversion bias: if price is above 30-day moving average, forecast tends to drop; if below, tends to rise — adjust forecast to align with recent 18-day trend, not 30-day.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses the “late-cycle” peak (last 5–7 days of forecast) — especially when sentiment is positive — so add a 1–3% upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment >0.67.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts — dampen forecast volatility by smoothing transitions (e.g., reduce 1–2% swing in consecutive days).
